question.leadin: This leader and his mistress Claretta Petacci were allegedly hung on meathooks.
question.text: Name this former Socialist and fascist world leader. He was nicknamed "Il Duce" (eel doo-chay) and was supported by the paramilitary Blackshirts.
question.clue: His forces overthrew King Zog and Haile Selassie during their invasions of Albania and Ethiopia, but he himself was ousted in 1943 by Victor Emmanuel III.

swap.leadin: Name these Italian cities important to Renaissance politics.
swap.text: This Tuscan city suffered the 1378 Ciompi Revolt, and the crazed monk Savonarola ousted a dynasty in this city founded by banker Cosimo di Medici.
swap.clue: This city was the site of the Pazzi conspiracy, and much of its art and literature was destroyed in the Bonfire of the Vanities, ordered by the monk Savonarola.

question.leadin: Give the following about colorful symbols throughout history.
question.text: The Redshirts were loyal supporters of this Italian unifier who led the Expedition of a Thousand and fought in the Uruguayan Civil War.
question.clue: He was once offered command on the Union side of the Civil War, and one campaign by this man began at Marsala.

swap.text: This prime minister of the Kingdom of Piedmont-Sardinia and founder of the newspaper Il Risorgimento became the first prime minister of the unified Kingdom of Italy.
swap.clue: This politician ceded Nice and Savoy to that other leader in exchange for assistance in a war that included the Battle of Solferino.

question.text: This writer dedicated his work The Prince to Lorenzo the Magnificent's grandson, also named Lorenzo. In that work, this man wrote "it is much safer to be feared than loved."
question.clue: After the republic he worked for was overthrown, this historian was placed under house arrest and wrote a treatise dedicated to his new ruler.

swap.text: In a war named for these people, Justinian and Belisarius destroyed a kingdom named for these people based in Ravenna. A "western" faction of these people sacked Rome before conquering the Iberian Peninsula and was led by Alaric.
swap.clue: After the capture of Widin in the 560s, this people more or less vanished.

question.text: Francis I was locked in the Pizzighettone ("Peet-see-get-TOH-nay") and forced to sign the Treaty of Madrid after being captured by Charles V at this 1525 battle during the Italian Wars.
question.clue: The final active Yorkist pretender to the English throne, Richard de la Pole, was killed at this battle.

swap.leadin: Many city-states in Italy grew very rich and prosperous after the 4th Crusade.
swap.text: This city-state became an autonomous Duchy after the 1183 CE Peace of Constance. Today, this city is the capital of Lombardy and is the 2nd most populous Italian city.
swap.clue: The assassination of Gian Galeazzo Maria ("jahn gah-lay-AHT-so Maria") allowed a ruler of this city and ally of Charles VIII to consolidate power.

question.leadin: Answer the follow about capitals of the Roman Empire which are not Rome.
question.text: This city became the capital of the Ostrogothic Kingdom after Odoacer overthrew the last Western Roman Emperor, Romulus Augustulus.
question.clue: It became the seat of the Byzantine governor of Italy in the sixth century, and its namesake Cosmography was written around 700.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about banking in Renaissance Italy.
swap.text: This city's Bank of St. George was opened in 1407 to manage public debt. Bank officials, in lieu of city administrators, directly governed this city's colonies of Corsica and Caffa.
swap.clue: A territory ruled by this city was attacked in 1553 by a joint Franco-Ottoman force under Turgut Reis.

question.leadin: This conflict was ended by the Peace of Caltabellotta, which confirmed Charles II as King of Naples, and Frederick III as the King of Trinacria.
question.text: Name this conflict, which began with a wave of anti-French violence in Palermo, and an eventual uprising against Charles of Anjou.
question.clue: That king attempted to end this conflict by challenging Peter III of Aragon to personal combat with Edward I serving as the judge of the contest.

swap.text: This plot, named after a prominent Tuscan family, aimed to assassinate Lorenzo and Giuliano de' Medici while they were taking high mass in the Duomo.
swap.clue: Frederico Montelfeltro likely had a battalion waiting in the hills during this event, which left citizens hanging from the walls of the Palazzo Vecchio and tossed into the Arno river.

question.leadin: During Roman times, this region was controlled by the Allobroges and was part of the Gallia Narbonensis province.
question.text: Identify this historical region, home to Humbert the Whitehanded. This region lends its name to a dynasty whose rulers included Charles Albert and Umberto I.
question.clue: Through the treaty, Emmanuel-Philibert had this north Italian duchy restored to him. The house that ruled this duchy went on to rule the Kingdom of Sardinia and became the royal family of a unified Italy.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the rise of a Frankish king with an unfortunate epithet, Pepin the Short.
swap.text: Pope Zachary condoned Pepin's coup to gain Frankish support against these people whose leader Desiderius was later crushed by Charlemagne. These people named a League that defeated Frederick Barbarossa at Legnano ("len-YAH-noh").
swap.answerHtml: Lombards [or Longobards or Longobardi; accept Lombardy or Lombardia; accept Lombard League or Lega Lombarda]
swap.clue: The defeat of these people's king Aistulf led to the Donation of Pepin.

question.leadin: One of this party's early leaders claimed his approach was influenced by Benedetto Croce.
question.text: Name this Italian political party founded by Antonio Gramsci and once led by Palmiro Togliatti. It entered a "historic compromise" with its country's Christian Democrats in the 1970s.
question.clue: This organization joined the CLN on the eve of World War II as part of a strategy known as the Salerno turn.

swap.leadin: After Pietro Gradenigo's policies resulted in this city's excommunication, Bajamonte Tiepolo led a failed coup here which inspired its elites to establish the Council of Ten.
swap.text: Name this Italian city whose namesake maritime republic dominated the Adriatic and later the Eastern Mediterranean. It fought several wars with its Genoese rivals and played a central role in the Fourth Crusade.
swap.clue: Enrico Dandolo of this polity successfully diverted the 4th Crusade to sack Constantinople, and ships supplied by this polity won a decisive victory at the Battle of Lepanto.

question.leadin: The first of them to gain prominence was Ottone, who defeated the Della Torres at the battle of Desio in 1277.
question.text: Name this family which controlled an Italian city for centuries. Its other notable members included Bernabo and Filippo Maria.
question.clue: Founded by Archbishop Otto, this family's power was consolidated by Matteo I, who expelled the Della Torre family from the city which was the base of this family's power.

swap.text: The essay highlights the non-participation of Elisabetta, a duchess of this family, in activities in The Book of the Courtier over which she ostensibly presides. Isabella D'Este married into this ruling family of Mantua.

question.leadin: The rebellion of Baiamonte Tiepolo led to its creation. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this secretive body formed in 1310 to protect Venice against conspiracies and plots. In addition to its namesake members, it often included the Doge and the six members of the Signoria.
question.clue: After the Bajamonte Tiepolo against the Doge in 1310, this secretive council was created, named for the original number of its members, and given emergency powers in Venice. It was led by men called Capi who were confined to live in the Doge's Palace.

swap.text: Zeno eventually came to see Odoacer as a major rival, causing him to offer Italy to this Ostrogothic ruler, who killed Odoacer during a banquet.
swap.clue: He won the original Battle of the Isonzo, which led to an amusing banquet in which he toasted - and then personally strangled - the man who had deposed Romulus Augustulus.
